channel.title: Via Fidelitatis — Faithful FI for Catholic Families
channel.description: Practical financial independence tools and faith-filled stewardship insights for Catholic families.

item.title: Open the Mantle: Lessons from St. Nicholas of Tolentino
item.description: When the prior stopped him, the bread under St. Nicholas’s mantle turned to roses. Families that keep a real surplus can open the same hand without counting the cost.

item.title: Begin in the Small: Lessons from Mary's Nativity
item.description: Joachim and Anne received the child in an ordinary house after long waiting. Families that keep the cradle and the budget small leave room for the grace that arrives quietly and grows without fanfare.

item.title: Cut the Royal Hair: Lessons from St. Cloud
item.description: Cloud cut his long royal hair before the bishop, renouncing the Frankish throne. Families that cut the claim on every extra dollar free surplus for vocation and the poor.

item.title: Leave the Court for the Cave: Lessons from St. Rosalia
item.description: Rosalia left the Palermo court and carved her resolution on the cave wall. Families that trade lifestyle inflation for a simpler rule gain the quiet margin prayer and mercy actually need.

item.title: Pay the Debt of Justice: Lessons from St. Gregory the Great
item.description: Gregory sold the family estates and founded monasteries. Surplus left in checking is already owed — when we meet the needy we pay a debt of justice, not offer a gift.

item.title: Books We Keep in the House
item.description: A short shelf we actually reread — not a coffee-table stack. Six TAN titles that train ordered love, detachment, and a household rule of prayer.

item.title: Give the Windfall a Job: Lessons from St. Ingrid
item.description: A raise sits in checking, then becomes a nicer kitchen. Give the windfall a job first — give, buffer, invest — the way St. Ingrid gave her fortune a vocation.

item.title: Purchasing Is a Moral Act: Lessons from Creation Day
item.description: Most budgets treat “we can afford it” as permission. Naming “enough” makes the purchase a moral act and frees surplus for the poor and the vocation.

item.title: Give Away the Horse: Lessons from St. Aidan
item.description: St. Aidan gave away the king’s horse the same day he received it. Raises and extras are for mercy, not a heavier life.

item.title: He Must Increase: Lessons from St. John the Baptist
item.description: He must increase; we must decrease. Shrink the lifestyle, not the vocation, so there is room to tell the truth and share the surplus.
